Rule Name: Prevent Ownership Share Double Counting in Multi-Client Contract Relationships
Rule / Expected Result:
When ownership-share information from song_share_summary_mv is combined with client and contract information from tempo_active_song_rate_client_v, the resulting dataset must preserve the intended reporting grain. Publisher mechanical, performance, and synchronization percentages should not be multiplied by the number of active client relationships associated with the same contract.

Expected result:

Each controlled ownership interest should be counted once at the appropriate reporting grain.
Aggregate controlled shares for a song, territory, writer, or contract should not increase solely because multiple clients are attached to the same contract.
Total publisher percentages should remain consistent regardless of the number of associated clients.
Business Context / Rule:
tempo_active_song_rate_client_v is maintained at a song-client-contract relationship grain and may contain multiple active client rows for a single contract. song_share_summary_mv is maintained at a song-territory-writer-contract ownership grain.

Directly joining these objects without first reconciling grain differences can create a many-to-many relationship where the same ownership interest is repeated once for every associated client. This results in overstated publisher mechanical, performance, and synchronization percentages.

When ownership reporting is required:

Ownership information should first be aggregated to the intended reporting grain.
Client and contract information should be summarized separately.
The aggregated datasets should then be joined using compatible business keys.

This rule is particularly important for LATAM reporting, client ownership reporting, contract qualification reporting, and any report utilizing Song IP Territory or Song Contract Territory ownership percentages.
Notes:
Failure to comply with this rule may result in:

Overstated controlled shares
Incorrect ownership reporting
Misstated repertoire control percentages
Inaccurate licensing and rights-management analysis
Duplicate ownership values appearing for songs with multiple clients linked to the same contract

Rule Name: ACK Status vs Validation Message Interpretation
Rule / Expected Result: ACK Status Codes determine the high-level operational registration outcome. Validation Messages should be used together with ACK Status Codes to understand the reason for the outcome. Business Context / Rule: ACK Status Codes indicate what happened during recipient processing (Accepted, Rejected, Conflict, No Participation, Duplicate, etc.). The corresponding Validation Message provides the underlying reason for the outcome and should be reviewed during registration investigations, exception management, root-cause analysis, and reporting.
Notes: Related to cwr_details_message_v. ACK Status Codes represent outcome. Validation Messages represent explanation. RM and XX represent manual resolution statuses and should not be interpreted as recipient-issued rejection outcomes.

Rule / Expected Result: Validation messages stored in song_ack_message_tx should be interpreted as structured CWR MSG records rather than free-text comments. Messages should be parsed into Record Type, Message Severity, Validation Number, and Message Text whenever detailed diagnostics or reporting is required.
Business Context / Rule: The CWR standard defines MSG records as structured validation outputs. Tempo stores MSG information as a concatenated string and does not persist the individual MSG components separately. Consistent parsing allows registration teams, analysts, and AI tools to identify validation failures, recipient-specific issues, and registration processing exceptions.
Notes:
Example: SPT:T009:TIS Numeric Code was not entered or was not found in the TIS database.

Parsed Structure:
SPT = Record Type
T = Transaction Rejected
009 = Validation Rule Number
Remaining text = Recipient explanation

Tempo stores the complete MSG structure within song_ack_message_tx and parsing is required to expose individual components.
